# Calculator procedures and measurement reference

```{=latex}
\markright{R01 Casio fx-991ES PLUS C}
```

## R01 Casio fx-991ES PLUS C procedures

| Task | Key sequence | Check |
|:--|:--|:--|
| general calculation | `MODE` `1` (`COMP`) | standard arithmetic mode |
| scientific entry | coefficient, `×10ˣ`, exponent | use the dedicated negative-sign key |
| engineering display | calculate, then `ENG` | each press changes exponent by 3 |
| reuse result | begin with operator or insert `Ans` | keeps the displayed result |
| fixed decimals | `SHIFT` `MODE`, `6`, digits | changes display rounding |
| scientific display | `SHIFT` `MODE`, `7`, digits | controls displayed significant digits |
| normal display | `SHIFT` `MODE`, `8`, `2` | keeps small values in decimal form longer |
| solve | `MODE` `1`, equation in $X$, `SHIFT` `CALC` | may return one of several roots |
| table | `MODE` `7`, enter $f(X)$, start, end, step | use for trend checking |
| base conversion | `MODE` `4`, choose `DEC`, `HEX`, `BIN`, or `OCT` | checks hand conversions |

**Discipline:** Keep the full calculator result through intermediate work. Round once, report units, and include a complete answer sentence.

Official reference: [Casio fx-570ES PLUS and fx-991ES PLUS User's Guide](https://www.casio.com/content/dam/casio/global/support/manuals/calculators/pdf/004-en/f/fx-570_991ES_PLUS_EN.pdf).

## R02 Measurement and evidence cycle

Use the same cycle throughout the curriculum:

1. Predict the direction and approximate magnitude.
2. Calculate using GUESS.
3. Draw a proper schematic or block diagram.
4. Simulate or verify.
5. Build or test where appropriate.
6. Compare expected and observed results.
7. Diagnose a fault or limitation.
8. Explain and reflect.

| Evidence category | Successful work shows |
|:--|:--|
| mathematical reasoning and GUESS | correct relationships, units, precision, and conclusion |
| schematic quality | standard symbols, labels, values, junctions, and readable layout |
| simulation or verification | correct construction, measurements, comparison, and limitations |
| physical construction | safe practice, organized wiring, and pre-power checks |
| testing and troubleshooting | expected readings, evidence-based diagnosis, and verification |
| design decisions | criteria, trade-offs, and justified changes |
| documentation | clear tables, graphs, images, captions, and engineering conclusion |

The quick reference contains the compact formulas. The electronics library contains notes, staged slides, assignments, simulations, labs, and restricted teacher materials.
